name: Non-malignant and Non-cirrhotic Portal Vein Thrombosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Non-malignant and Non-cirrhotic Portal Vein Thrombosis

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of portal vein thrombosis without signs of malignancy or cirrhosis
No clinical, laboratory, or imaging evidence of liver cirrhosis
Exclusion of underlying malignancy as cause of portal vein thrombosis
Presence of clinical signs such as abdominal pain or portal hypertension symptoms
Evidence of prothrombotic state or coagulation abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological confirmation of portal vein thrombosis without evidence of malignancy or cirrhosis is required.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of cirrhosis and malignancy by clinical, laboratory, and imaging studies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Acute abdominal pain localized to the right upper quadrant
searchTerms: sharp pain in right upper belly

pathognomonic.symptomName: Splenomegaly detected on physical examination or imaging
searchTerms: enlarged spleen found on exam or scan
splenomegaly detected physically or by imaging

common.symptomName: Gastrointestinal bleeding secondary to portal hypertension
searchTerms: bleeding in digestive tract from portal pressure
GI bleeding due to portal hypertension
blood in stool from liver pressure
fluid in abdomen without liver scarring
reduced blood clotting cells from hypersplenism
tiredness from high portal vein pressure
weakness due to increased portal pressure
mild yellow skin without liver scarring

rare.symptomName: Hepatic encephalopathy in absence of cirrhosis
searchTerms: brain dysfunction from liver failure without cirrhosis
portal vein blocked with collateral vessels

laboratory: Thrombocytopenia and leukopenia due to hypersplenism
Elevated D-dimer and fibrin degradation products
Normal liver function tests without synthetic dysfunction
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing portal vein thrombosis
Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI confirming portal vein occlusion without cirrhotic liver changes
Absence of hepatic nodules or masses suggestive of malignancy
genetic: Possible inherited thrombophilia mutations (e.g., Factor V Leiden, prothrombin gene mutation)
other: Endoscopy revealing esophageal or gastric varices due to portal hypertension

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of underlying hepatocellular carcinoma or other malignancy
Imaging evidence of tumor invasion into portal vein
Clinical and imaging evidence of liver cirrhosis

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain with signs of intestinal ischemia
Rapid progression of portal hypertension with massive gastrointestinal bleeding
Signs of liver failure or encephalopathy without known cirrhosis
references: Ageno W, et al. Portal vein thrombosis: clinical and laboratory features and outcome. Thromb Res. 2010.
Condat B, et al. Portal vein thrombosis in adults: risk factors, clinical presentation and outcome. J Hepatol. 2000.
